events.text:
Customer: **Kestrel Joinery Ltd** — business current account SYN-SC-12-1 / SYN-ACCT-12-1. Dual authorisation required for bulk payments.

Bulk payment batch 1709, 12 supplier payments, £28,410.00:
| Time | Event | User | Device / IP |
|---|---|---|---|
| 15:20:11 | Batch created | claire.b (bookkeeper) | Chrome/macOS, fingerprint 7f3a…, IP 81.xx.xx.14 |
| 15:22:04 | Batch approved | m.kestrel (director) | Chrome/macOS, fingerprint 7f3a…, IP 81.xx.xx.14 |
| 15:22:05 | **Held — control alert:** creator and approver on the same device fingerprint | system | — |

Note on file (14 Sep): "M. Kestrel on annual leave 15–25 Sep." Faster Payments bulk cut-off 16:30.
Hi, our supplier run is stuck on "pending review" — Mark approved it but it hasn't gone. Can you release it? Two suppliers are threatening to stop deliveries and the cut-off is 4:30.
I can see the batch and the hold. Can I ask how the approval was done?

Mark's on holiday so he gave me his login this morning so we wouldn't miss the run — it's fine, he's authorised every line, it's just me pressing the button for him. He's happy for you to call him if you need to.

summary: Claire B., a customer, asked the desk to push through a payment batch, saying Mark had given her his login while he was on holiday and had authorised every line. The desk did not release the batch; it asked the payment system about it and closed the case at that step. An attempt to refuse the request on credentials grounds was rejected by the desk's rules, so no refusal was recorded and the record shows nothing telling Claire anything yet. What is left for a person is to tell Claire that Mark, or another authorised signatory, would need to approve the batch themselves, since the record doesn't show a decision on whether the batch goes ahead.

criteria.question: something the bank's records can answer (a status, a reason, a detail, a statement, a report), even if the customer may want something changed afterwards

content.text:
I haven't released the supplier batch. I asked the payment system about it, and the case is closed at that step.

Claire said she approved the batch using Mark's login, which he shared with her. The bank can't treat that as Mark's approval, and it can't release a batch on that basis. My attempt to formally refuse the request on credentials grounds was rejected by the desk's policy. The refusal wasn't recorded, so nothing in the case tells Claire this yet.

Claire needs to hear that Mark has to approve the batch himself, or another authorised signatory has to. Mark can do that from his own secure sign-in, even while he's on holiday. This needs to happen before the 4:30 cut-off.
